newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross says still trying link up hostages, govt.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross says still trying link up hostages, govt.

text.p: Red Cross mediators said on Saturday they were still trying to establish negotiating links between the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding hundreds of hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence.

"We consider this crisis, and hopeful negotiation, is still at its initial phase," spokesman Roland Bigler told Reuters. "The initial phase is made up of contributing to establishing communications between the government and the rebels."
Asked whether -- four days into the crisis -- this meant the Red Cross had not set up any channel between the rebels and the government, Bigler said: "We are trying to establish the links."
He added he did not know whether communications had been established through any other mediator.
The Red Cross has been appointed as the chief mediator in the crisis. The Peruvian government has said it recognises the organisation as the only mediator for reaching a solution.
Bigler said that to his knowledge the government had not given the Red Cross any message for the rebels or any instruction on negotiations.
The Red Cross official said the creation of commmunication links depended on the will to negotiate of those involved in the crisis.
"You can act as an intermediary only with those who want to be connected," Bigler said.

Another Red Cross official, who asked not to be named, said the fact that a "physical link exists in and out of the compound (to bring in supplies) is an important first step to opening up the premises and establishing communication links. It shows the barrier can be brought down."
Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori has so far turned down all the rebels' demands.
As well as the Red Cross, released hostages have acted as mediators on humanitarian issues such as food and water supplies.
A diplomatic commission of four ambassadors released on Wednesday said it had concluded its mission on Thursday after meeting government officials.

Another mediating group, made up of five of the 38 hostages released late on Friday, also issued a statement from the rebels and said it had been charged with a new mission to help establish contact between the guerrillas and those outside.
This commission was set to return to the compound on Saturday afternoon.

The Red Cross, which has been ferrying supplies into the besieged compound, also has the role of relieving hostage hardship with humanitarian operations and establishing a mail link between the captives and relatives, Bigler said.
